title: Feat command output
description: The documents `feat` prints when it is asked for one with --json. It describes what this build prints and is held to the Go types by a test in both directions; what is promised about it is a separate decision (ADR-099).

note.description: Explains a value that would otherwise need explaining, such as a default Feat filled in or a file it does not read. It is empty when there is nothing to explain.

value.description: The resolved value as it will be used.

configuration_section.description: One titled block of resolved configuration.

fields.description: The block's values, in the order the table prints them.

agent_path.description: Where task worktrees are mounted in the agent's own container, empty for host-native execution.

default_access.description: The repository's default participation in a task.

id.description: Identifies the repository within the project.

primary.description: Whether this is the project's primary repository.

runtime_path.description: Where this repository's own services expect their source, empty for a repository whose code no service runs.

runtime_services.description: The services this repository asks Feat to manage.

fingerprint.description: Identifies this exact draft, and is what launching carries back.

notes.description: What happened while resolving that the user should know about without it stopping the task, such as a fetch that failed while an older remote-tracking ref was still available.

task.description: The draft as it is now recorded, carrying every resolved base and every proposed branch and worktree path.

execution.description: The isolated environment one agent session runs in.

container.description: The observed container, empty when none was observed.

health.description: The observed health, which is separate from running.

identity.description: What makes an action affect one task's environment and no other's, which for the Compose adapter is the project name.

observed_at.description: When the last four fields were established.

provider.description: Identifies the execution adapter, such as the Compose adapter.

running.description: Whether the environment was observed to be up.

service.description: The service the agent runs in.

status.description: What the environment itself called its state.

user.description: The identity the agent runs as, which is never root.

git_observation.description: What Feat last saw in a task worktree.

ahead.description: How many commits the task branch had that its base did not.

behind.description: How many commits the base had that the task branch did not.

changed_files.description: How many files differed from the recorded base commit.

dirty.description: Whether the worktree held uncommitted changes.

merged.description: Whether the task branch was contained in its base branch.

merge_request.description: A request Feat opened on a forge. GitHub calls it a pull request; there is one shape either way.

reference.description: The forge's own identifier for the merge request, as it printed it.

url.description: Where the merge request can be read.

port.description: One published port of one service.

host_ip.description: The address the container runtime reported the port bound on, empty when it reported none. It is read back rather than assumed, so a binding that disagrees with the allocation beside it can be seen.

host_port.description: The port it is published on.

port_allocation.description: One host port Feat reserved for one service of one task.

address.description: Where the service is reached from this machine, which is the value of its generated FEAT_HOST_URL variable without the scheme. It is not the address another container reaches it at: a published port belongs to the host's network namespace, and a service calling a sibling uses the Compose service name and the container port.

host_ip.description: The host address this port is published on: the one the project's own Compose file named, or the project's configured runtime.bind_address when it named none. It is empty only in a record written before Feat had a bind address of its own.

protocol.description: The protocol the publication is for, tcp or udp.

service.description: The service the port was reserved for.

project_configuration.description: The document `feat project show --json` prints: the configuration Feat will act on, after "~" expansion and after defaults are filled.

id.description: The project's identifier, which is also its configuration file's name.

name.description: The project's display name, which defaults to its identifier.

primary_repository.description: Where a task works by default.

repositories.description: Each repository's place on the host, in the agent's container, and in its own services' containers.

sections.description: The rest of the resolved configuration, in the order and the words the table prints: a dotted configuration path, the value Feat will use, and a note where one is needed.

publication.description: A task's recorded publication on the wire.

planned_at.description: When the publication was last planned.

repositories.description: One entry per repository the last publication planned, with what came of it.

updated_at.description: When any of its repositories last changed.

publication_repository.description: One repository's part of a recorded publication.

attempted_at.description: When publishing this repository was last attempted.

base_branch.description: The branch the merge request is opened against.

commit.description: The commit the approved text described and the push carried.

failure.description: Why this repository did not publish, in the words of whatever refused.

forge.description: Which forge the merge request is opened on.

remote.description: The Git remote the branch is pushed to.

repository_id.description: Identifies the repository within the project.

request.description: The merge request that was opened, present exactly while the state is published.

state.description: Planned, published, or failed. A planned entry is one this publication had not attempted when it stopped, which is what makes an interrupted publication recoverable rather than mysterious.

review.description: What is known about a task's work on the wire.

checks.description: The results, each attributed to whoever produced it.

gated.description: That a completion gate ran at least one of them. It is the difference between a verification and a claim about one.

requested_at.description: When the agent asked for review, or null if it has not.

summary.description: The agent's own account of what it did, which is a claim.

detail.description: What the check said about itself: the agent's words, or the tail of what the command printed.

id.description: The check's identifier, as the project configured it.

reporter.description: "agent" for a claimed result and "provider" for one a gate enforced.

repository_id.description: The repository the check ran in, empty for a project-wide check.

status.description: Passed, failed, skipped, or unknown. Unknown is a check that did not report — one that could not be started, or that ran out of time — and it is deliberately not a failure.

arguments.description: The argument vector, expanded by the daemon and never a shell string.

directory.description: The task worktree the command runs in, which is checked before it is returned and checked again before it is run.

program.description: The program to run, which is the project's own configuration.

repository_id.description: The repository the command runs in.

review_repository.description: One repository's comparison against its recorded base.

access.description: The access the task has to it: read_write or read_only.

ahead.description: Ahead, Behind, and Merged come from the last observation: ahead of the recorded base, behind the base ref as it is now, and contained in it.

base_commit.description: The immutable commit the task started from, which never moves.

base_ref.description: The ref the base policy named and BaseCommit is what it resolved to. The commit is what every comparison uses, for the whole life of the task (invariant 8).

behind.description: How many commits the base branch has that the task branch does not.

branch.description: The task's branch in this repository.

changed_files.description: Counts tracked and untracked files that differ from the base; Insertions and Deletions count tracked lines only.

deletions.description: Lines removed since the base commit.

dirty.description: Whether the worktree holds uncommitted changes.

head_commit.description: What the worktree has checked out, empty when the agent has not committed. Committing is optional (FR-GIT-007).

insertions.description: Lines added since the base commit.

merged.description: Whether the task branch is contained in its base branch.

repository_id.description: Identifies the repository within the project.

worktree_path.description: Where the task's worktree is on the host.

review_status.description: The response of every review action.

commands.description: The configured external commands, expanded for this task and checked. The client runs them with its own terminal.

notes.description: What a user should know: a repository that could not be read, a command that could not be expanded, or a count that means less than it looks like.

repositories.description: The per-repository comparisons, each against that repository's own recorded base commit (FR-REV-001).

review.description: The decision, the agent's summary, and the check results.

task.description: The task as it is now recorded.

allocations.description: The host ports Feat reserved for this task's reachable services, held until the runtime is destroyed. They are what the task will be published on; Ports is what the started containers turned out to publish, which is empty until something starts.

composition.description: Composition, StaticOverrides, EnvFiles, and the two generated paths are the exact inputs this runtime was created from, kept so that a later action reaches the same resources even if the project's configuration has since been edited. They are the user's own paths, which are not secrets; no value from an environment file is ever read, let alone published.

env_files.description: The environment files passed to Compose by path; no value in one is ever read.

generated_include_path.description: The document Feat wrote to join the repositories' own Compose files.

generated_override_path.description: The override Feat wrote for this task.

health.description: Separate from State: without a configured health check the honest answer is unknown.

identity.description: The unique runtime identity, which is what makes an action affect one task's services and no other's.

networks.description: And Volumes are what Compose reports as this project's. Volumes are listed because destroying a runtime retains every one of them, and a retained resource nobody can see is one nobody will remove.

observed_at.description: When the runtime was last observed.

ports.description: The publications the started containers turned out to have, empty until something starts.

provenance.description: Says where each managed service's code comes from. It is resolved from configuration and the project's own Compose files when the runtime is, so a service that will not run the task's work says so before anything is started rather than after.

provider.description: Identifies the runtime adapter, which in v0 is Docker Compose.

services.description: The services this task's runtime manages.

state.description: The observed state of the task's services.

static_overrides.description: The override files the project declares, by path.

volumes.description: The volumes Compose reports as this project's, which destroying a runtime retains.

runtime_service.description: One observed service of a task's runtime.

container.description: The observed container, empty when the service has none.

exit_code.description: The exit status of a service that has stopped.

health.description: The observed health, which is unknown without a configured health check.

managed.description: Whether the project's runtime.services names this one. A service that it does not name is one Compose started because a managed service depends on it; it belongs to this task's Compose project all the same, and Feat stops and removes it with the rest.

name.description: The service's name in the project's Compose files.

state.description: What the container runtime called it, and Status its own longer phrasing, kept verbatim so a client quotes the tool rather than paraphrasing it.

status.description: What the container runtime called the service's state, in its own words.

runtime_source.description: One repository's contribution to a task's application.

directory.description: The checkout its own Compose files' relative paths resolve against.

files.description: That repository's Compose files, in order.

repository.description: Identifies the repository within the project.

runtime_status.description: The response of every runtime action.

notes.description: What a user should know about what they just started, in Feat's terms rather than the container runtime's. They are observations of the running containers and are recomputed by the next action.

services.description: What was observed: one entry per configured service, so that a service with no container is reported as one — a runtime missing half its services is not a runtime that is running — followed by everything else in the task's Compose project, which is everything Compose started because a configured service depends on it.

task.description: The task as it is now recorded, carrying its runtime.

service_provenance.description: Where one managed service's code comes from.

baked.description: The repositories whose code reaches the service only through its image, so a change appears there once the image is built again and not before.

built.description: Whether the service's image is built from the task's work rather than mounted into it.

mounted.description: And Built are the repositories whose task worktree the service mounts, and whose task worktree its image is built from.

repositories.description: The repositories that asked Feat to manage the service.

runs_task_code.description: Whether any of the task's work reaches the service.

control_path.description: Where the agent's control files are, empty where there are none.

execution.description: The isolated environment the session runs in, or null when it runs on this host and there is nothing to identify.

execution_mode.description: Where the session runs: devcontainer or host.

last_activity_at.description: When Feat last saw the session do anything.

last_event_sequence.description: The last control event Feat processed.

process.description: The observed process state. Idle never means complete.

provider.description: The agent adapter running the session, which in v0 is Claude Code.

provider_session_id.description: The agent's own identifier when it exposes one.

tmux.description: Where the session's terminal is, by stable identifier.

source.description: Records where a task brief came from.

kind.description: Where the brief came from: prompt, markdown, or ticket.

reference.description: What it came from, which for a Markdown import is the file's path.

ticket.description: The ticket the brief was composed from, present exactly for a ticket source. It travels in both directions: a client composing a brief from a ticket sends what it read, and a task carries it back so that a caller can say which ticket the work came from.

attention.description: Records whether the user may need to intervene. It is separate from every other dimension on purpose.

failure.description: Why the task is in `failed`, and null in every other state. It travels with the state because a client that can show one and not the other can only report that something went wrong.

key.description: The human-facing short identifier derived from the ID.

project_id.description: The project the task belongs to.

publication.description: What the task has recorded about publishing — one entry per repository the last publication planned, with what came of it — or null for a task that has never published.

repositories.description: The repositories the task is bound to, with what each starts from.

runtime.description: The task's application runtime, or null when it has none.

session.description: The task's agent session, or null before it is launched.

verification.description: What the agent reported about its own checks, or null when it has reported none. It is the agent's claim rather than a result anything enforced, which is why the source is part of it.

task_failure.description: Why a task is in `failed`, in the words of whatever failed.

tasks.description: Every task the daemon knows about, archived ones included.

task_repository.description: Binds a task to one repository of its project.

access.description: The access the task has to it: read_write or read_only.

base_commit.description: The immutable recorded base. Review and cleanup compare against it for the lifetime of the task.

base_ref.description: The revision the base was resolved from, for a project whose base policy is explicit.

branch.description: The task's branch in this repository.

container_path.description: Where the worktree is mounted in the agent's environment, empty for host-native execution.

observation.description: The last observed Git state, or null if never observed.

repository_id.description: Identifies the repository within the project.

worktree_path.description: Where the task's worktree is on the host.

ticket_reference.description: The ticket a task's brief was composed from.

change_available.description: That the tracker has since shown something different from the snapshot.

provider.description: Which tracker the ticket came from, and is what the published shape's optional source fills.

reference.description: The ticket's own reference, exactly as the tracker command printed it.

snapshot.description: The ticket as it was when Feat read it.

url.description: Where the ticket can be read.

ticket_snapshot.description: The ticket as it was when Feat read it.

body.description: The ticket's body when Feat read it.

state.description: The ticket's state when Feat read it, in the tracker's own word.

taken_at.description: When the tracker command that printed it ran, which is what versions a snapshot: the published shape carries no revision of the tracker's own.

title.description: The ticket's title when Feat read it.

tmux.description: Locates a session's terminal. These are execution references, never task identity (invariant 10).

session.description: The tmux session identifier, never a display name.

socket.description: The tmux socket the session lives on, which is Feat's own.

window.description: The tmux window identifier, never an index.

verification.description: A task's check results, attributed to whoever produced them.

failed.description: How many of the agent's checks it reported as failing.

other.description: How many of the agent's checks it reported as neither passing nor failing.

passed.description: Passed, Failed, and Other count the results by outcome.

source.description: Who produced the results: "agent" for a result the agent claimed, "provider" for one a completion gate enforced. Only "agent" occurs in v0.1.

summary.description: The agent's account of what it did.
